script.source:
def apply(ctx):
    dmg = ctx.rand.roll("1d6")
    ctx.target.state.hp = ctx.target.state.hp - dmg
    ctx.emit("hit", target=ctx.target, reach=1, dmg=dmg)
    return dmg

def tick(ctx):
    me = ctx.self
    st = me.state
    dest = st.haunt if me.parent.id == st.home else st.home
    ctx.move(me, dest)
    ctx.emit("arrived", target=dest, reach=-1, who=me.id, place=dest)
    ctx.say(ctx.rand.choice(st.lines))

script.source:
def apply(ctx):
    text = ctx.target.state.text or "nothing is written on it"
    ctx.emit("read", target=ctx.target, reach=0, text=text)
    ctx.log(text)
    return text

def on(ctx, event):
    # installed on the world root with set_rule, so it hears every event; the stage lives on the Story entity
    story = ctx.find(type="story", limit=1)[0]
    st = story.state
    stage = st.stage
    k = event.kind
    if stage == "start" and k == "arrived" and event.payload.get("place") == st.landing:
        ctx.emit("scene", target=st.landing, reach=1,
                 text="Cold mist lifts off the river. The raft is moored and the bell rope on the post hangs cut. No ferryman.")
        ctx.patch(story, {"stage": "ask"})
    elif stage == "ask" and k == "talked" and event.target == st.mara:
        about = str(event.payload.get("about", "")).lower()
        if "ferry" in about or "tam" in about or "cross" in about or "river" in about:
            # patch merges: this adds one topic to Mara's table without touching the rest
            ctx.patch(ctx.get(st.mara), {"dialog": {
                "bell": "The landing bell calls him down from wherever he is sleeping it off. Rope was cut by the Pell boys. Hob at the mill keeps rope."}})
            ctx.patch(story, {"stage": "bell"})
    elif stage in ("ask", "bell") and k == "rang":
        tam = ctx.get(st.tam)
        ctx.patch(tam, {"hidden": False})
        ctx.move(tam, st.landing)
        ctx.emit("scene", target=st.square, reach=1, text="Far off, a hoarse voice answers the bell.")
        ctx.emit("scene", target=st.landing, reach=1, text="Old Tam comes down the reed path, rubbing his eyes, and steps onto the raft.")
        ctx.patch(story, {"stage": "cross"})
    elif stage == "cross" and k == "crossed":
        ctx.emit("scene", target=st.far_bank, reach=1, text="The raft grinds onto the far shingle. Behind you Ashford is a handful of lights in the fog.")
        ctx.patch(ctx.root(), {"story": "complete"})
        ctx.patch(story, {"stage": "done"})

memory.text: Traveler found Tam at the mill with Biscuit trailing. Thanked me, says they owe me one: I said a story, no coin. Promised three ales when they come back this way.
The Traveler: polite, kept to the one ale deal, found Tam and the dog, and went down to the Landing in the morning. Owes me a story. Three ales waiting if they come back.

state.description: The wheel turns slow in the mill race. Flour dust on everything. Rope, sacks and a sleeping dog.
Shingle and a path going up into the dark. The village is behind you now.

A muddy path round the back of the mill drops into tall reeds along the mill race. The ground is soft and wet, and the reeds are flattened in places where somebody has lain down. The light is going grey.
A packed-earth square between the inn, the well and the road down to the river. Early morning; grey light, the inn lamps out, last night's fog gone off the river.
Pole-and-rope raft, moored to the post.

state.text: FERRY: dawn to dusk, ring for Tam. NO CROSSINGS IN FOG. Pell's Mill buying barley. Lost: one grey dog, answers to Biscuit, does not come when called.

state.description: Heavy. Why would you.
Stone well with a wooden lid and a bench beside it, worn pale where people sit.
A plank bench by the well. Something under it.
A heap of empty flour sacks in the warm corner behind the millstones, out of the draught. Dusty, but dry and soft enough to sleep on.
A river village at dusk. The ferryman is missing. Cross before the fog closes in.

payload.text: Tam was here till the second jug. Went off to sleep it off in the reeds behind the mill, I'd guess.
Tam cracks one eye. 'Mmh? Who's that. Not the bell, nobody rang the bell.' He tries to sit up and the reeds win. '...Inside. Aye. Fog's no place for a man's bones. Give us a hand up, then.'

Tam blinks at the sacks, then at you, and a slow grin comes up through the stubble. 'Morning. Aye. Now there's a word I like. Nobody crosses in fog anyhow, the board says so.' He lowers himself onto the far end of the heap with a groan. 'First light, you shake me, and I'll pole you over before Mara's even up. Mind the dog doesn't take the warm spot.'

Tam comes up out of sleep swinging at nothing, then sees it's you and the light, and lets his arm drop. 'First light. Aye. I said that, didn't I.' He pats his coat, front and back, and comes up empty. 'Food? Not a crumb on me, friend, I drank my supper. Hob'll have a heel of bread somewhere, he always does. Ask him nice and don't mention my jugs.'
That's Biscuit. Not mine. Nobody's, till somebody feeds him.
Hob looks at the dog, then at Tam on his sacks, and sighs through his nose. He fishes in his apron. 'Heel of yesterday's loaf. It's that or nothing. And if he's yours now, you take him with you.'
You do, love, and I'll take it as a story, not coin. Fog's off the river and Tam's on his feet, so go while he still is. Come back this way and the three I promised are waiting.
Let's go, boys.

dialog.dog: That's Biscuit. He'll follow anyone with a bone.
dialog.drink: Mara puts a hand flat over the tap. 'I said one. I've seen what a second does to folk who need the river tonight. Come back across in the morning and I'll pour you three.'
dialog.ferry: Tam's not been back since noon. Went up to the mill to drink with Hob and that was that. If you need across you need him, and the bell is the way to call him.
dialog.fog: River fog comes in with the dark. Nobody crosses blind. Take a light.
dialog.forget: Mara puts a hand flat over the tap. 'I said one. I've seen what a second does to folk who need the river tonight. Come back across in the morning and I'll pour you three.'
dialog.hob: Hob Pell runs the mill. Decent man, terrible sons.
dialog.lantern: There's a lantern on the post at the landing. You'll want something to light it with.
dialog.light: You'll want a tinderbox for that. Here, I keep a spare.
dialog.mill: Mara reads the worry on your face and softens a little. 'It's only up the hill. If Tam's there he's asleep, not dead. Shake him hard; he's had worse.' She glances at the sky. 'Don't dawdle. And come back past me before you go down to the water. You'll want a light, and I've got one.'
dialog.pay: She waves your hand away. 'Keep it. Pay me by getting over that water before the fog does. I don't want you sleeping on my bench.'
dialog.river: Mara laughs once, short. 'The Ash, love. Down the road past the Landing. You walked in here asking how to get over it, or near enough. That ale went straight to your head.' She nods down the hill. 'Ferry's the only way across, and the ferryman's gone missing.'
dialog.tam: Old Tam rows the ferry. Drinks at the mill. Sleeps where he falls.

payload.text: Thanks a lot, Mara. Thanks for your help. I owe you one.
Traveler found Tam at the mill with Biscuit trailing. Thanked me, says they owe me one: I said a story, no coin. Promised three ales when they come back this way.
The Traveler: polite, kept to the one ale deal, found Tam and the dog, and went down to the Landing in the morning. Owes me a story. Three ales waiting if they come back.
'Tam owes me for three jugs.'
